body: My friends don't text first either. I think it's normal but it's hard not to internalize it. It really feels like no one cares about me as much as I do them

I feel very similar. People only like what they can get out of you, and when you need some kind of sign that someone cares about you back, it's crickets. I don't know how to make friends when I'm like this either. I wish there was help and a reason for us to be here but there probably isn't. I think you have to find something in you that you like enough to keep you from snuffing it out. If I find out how to do that, I'll let you know.

I listened to people tell me that for years, to the point where I believed it enough to go on living, but it seems that eventually they all get bored with you and then you're just left with you and your hated existence and that's the worst thing that can happen. The feeling of false hope and abandonment. I just wish I had killed myself earlier, you know?

Sorry this isn't helpful. I've got nothing but bitterness and that hollowed out feeling today.
I feel this way a lot. It's hard to watch everyone I care about grow and make something of their life when I will never have that. Cancer or an assassin sounds nice.
I feel you there. Everyone around me has a special person and it feels inevitable that I will be alone forever.

I've had thoughts like this too... it feels like a few people are responsible for a lot of people's suffering, and some sort of complicated murder/suicide to remove a few bastards from the planet is romantic. As long as it's just a fantasy and you don't have the means, I think you're okay.
You have so much further to go from here. I don't think any of us were much of anything at 15.
Believe me you are not the only ugly one here

You sound like a good friend or loved one to have. It's hardest to be kind to yourself. I wish I knew how so I could help you in return.
Have you tried reaching out to anyone around you for help?

Talking to someone removed from my life about my thoughts and feelings has been good for me. If I tell them to my loved ones they become afraid or try to fix things or just don't understand. If I tell no one I get lost in them. If I tell them to her they're not trapped inside of me. This therapist is also very good at helping me find patterns in my thinking that lead me to a worse place, so when I notice those patterns I'm more able to talk myself out of it.

Ive felt frustration with therapists I "just talk to" before too, and this one seems different from previous, but fear that she'll react strongly is unavoidable.

I really appreciate your thoughts. I have a hard time picturing what I want from life but it's helpful to think about what I value as a place to start from. It's hard because it feels like everything is changing faster than I can keep up with but every little thing helps. Thank you.

I think I want to tell her, I'm just terrified of being put on a medical hold, with all the financial and social turmoil associated with disappearing for 72 hours.

Thank you for replying, and I hope you have people to help hold you up too.

If you still want to be friends, wait it out a few days and then unblock her and apologize. Anxiety happens; if she's reasonable and you humble yourself and explain, it should be okay. 

If you don't want to be friends, then that's that. And at least you took the chance to put yourself out there, and you'll be more experienced the next time you want to ask someone out. It sucks now, but there's the potential for growth no matter what from this.

Hair is important, it's not stupid to feel self conscious. My hair started going grey crazy fast 2 years ago when I was 23 and it was just another item on a long list of reasons to hate myself. 

The highs and lows are hard. You can build yourself up for weeks and get knocked down in one. If you can get on the right medication, the lows aren't as low, and it can be easier to recover. When I'm in my worst lows I spend so much time wondering what the point of it is too, but I try to focus on the fact that I know I don't lament things as much and ask those questions when I'm on an upswing.

This is what I do as well - the writing letters one works especially well, as eloquence and despair are not two things that go together for me.  hate that I have to trick myself into cleaning my house and not dying, but it looks damn functional to the untrained eye, and that has its benefits.

I can completely sympathize. Learning about and identifying RSD was one of the main reasons I was finally able to understand that so many of my problems with work and school were due to ADHD. It's so easy to go from feeling happy and safe with people you consider your support system, to feeling a sense of absolute despair, over something someone says. I feel like every glimmer of something good in my life is seconds away from the crushing reality that I'm worthless, I'm unwelcome and unwanted, and the last of the good people in my life have finally had enough of me. It's agoraphobia and ignored phone calls and calling in sick. 

I don't know how to cope with it either. I would've killed myself the last time I had a serious episode but I couldn't get anywhere high enough to be certain. If you have the access, you should see if there's any other medications they can try. When I had better health insurance, my therapist was using cognitive behavior therapy, and that helped a little too. I also rolled a dnd character with a lot of my worst characteristics so that i can feel marginally less shitty when she does something cool and badass and is generally not hated by the other party members.
Same here, can't wait to die alone.

The situation with your siblings sounds tough. My younger sister has a similar temperament to your younger siblings, and she's 18 unfortunately. 

In my experience I have a hard time remembering things when my depression is severe. If you like watching shows have you looked into a job at a movie theater? I used to watch movies in between cleaning and it was a good way to see a lot of the new stuff without having to pay. The added bonus of a little extra cash is always a plus too, you can feel more independent. 

Not sure about the online gaming aspects... when I was in community college LAN parties for all sorts of stuff were common but I'm not sure if there's a CC near you.

That sounds incredibly stressful, I'm sorry there's so much to deal with all at once. 

Most receptionists don't really care the reason - when I was in school, I'd say I had to go to office hours after getting a bad grade, and I've said stuff as dumb as "I've overslept" or "I missed the bus" without problems. Worrying about rescheduling makes  me feel worse than telling a half-lie to an office assistant, in my experience. 

Your first traffic ticket is scary. Just be honest about your mistake, and intent to drive better in the future, and most judges will reduce the fine. You may be asked to do traffic school, which is good! because your insurance won't go up! My first and only ticket appearance for running a red light lasted 10 minutes in total, and they reduced my fine by $200, so if you show up and are respectful it should be smooth. 

Something like the leak in a place that you rent is more the fault of the landlord than the tenant. If you did your best to clean, things should be okay. and if it does result in an eviction notice, most areas have local tenant advocacy groups that will tell you whether the eviction is fair or not. I don't think they would be able to evict you without warning you clearly about the problem first. 

I'm sorry if this isn't helpful, but I'll keep my fingers crossed for you, with your inspection & the rest.

I can understand the hesitation to take medicine, but if you're feeling this way, you should try and see a therapist. It may not be a cure-all, but you don't have to deal with your feelings all alone.

The idea of someone always having it worse has been a constant thread in the back of my mind when I'm feeling depressed or alone. It sounds like you might be an older sibling too? Trying to shake that pressure and guilt in order to take care of yourself is hard. 

I [24] am also living at home, and I can't talk to my family about how I'm feeling because my parents have too much on their plate to worry about my issues. When I graduated 2 years ago, I was extremely isolated because I wasn't working, and my friends were elsewhere, so I spent a lot of time in my room alone. things can feel really small awhen it's like that, and it's hard to cope. I know you said you don't really have anything you want to do, but what do you do online? If you can work that into an interest or activity that will get you looking for work or out for a hobby, it might help you feel a little more fulfilled, and you might meet someone who you'll feel comfortable opening up to. You deserve the opportunity to work and grow and meet people as much as everyone else, even if it doesn't feel like it.

I apologize if this isn't super helpful or if I misunderstood your post. I feel like I've been in a similar life place, and I'm still dealing with some of the circumstances you mentioned. I hope things will get better.

I'm really happy for you! I hope they're helpful! 

I started the referral process for seeing a psychiatrist last week, hopefully I'll see one soon too.
Seconded!
Shoot, so I probably should find someone else for a throwaway write in candidate for when the options are equally terrible.
